--- title: "Virginia DJJ Data File Codebooks" format: html --- **Data Sample:** * Juvenile intake complaints with intake dates from July 1, 2015 - June 30, 2021 * Dispositions – all dispositions for the intake complaints in the sample. * Caseload – all intake complaints in the sample that are associated with a workload status for diversion - "Diversion At Intake" or "Diversion Program Beyond 90 Days" **For all missing data plots**, here are the % missingness categories: "Good" <= 5% missing, "OK" <= 40% missing, "Bad" <= 80% missing, and "Remove" = 100% missing
This syntax pulls in all data files provided by DJJ stored as a series of Excel file tabs -- creates high-level codebooks for each using the DataExplorer package (https://boxuancui.github.io/DataExplorer/index.html). File names reflect the names provided by Dallas County.

### Intake Complaints, Fields Included ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Variable Description
juvenile_number A unique identification number that is automatically assigned at the time an electronic juvenile record is created in the electronic data management system.
case_number A unique identification number that is assigned to an intake case upon the creation of the intake.
offense_number A unique identification number that is automatically generated at the time an offense is entered in the electronic data management system.
csu The court service unit that opened the intake case.
fips_code The FIPS that opened the intake case.
date_opened Month and year of intake
intake_age Age at intake
pet_age Age at petition
sex The youth's sex assigned at birth.
race The youth's race.
hispanic The youth's ethnicity.
petitioner_type The type of individual who requested the petition for the case. In February 2015, petitioner type was expanded to include “School Resource Officer” (SRO) in addition to “School Official.” Previously, it was unclear if an SRO’s intake was marked as “School Official,” “Police Department,” or other.
petitioner_desc NA
intake_decision The decision made by the intake officer
prior_misd Prior number of misdemeanor complaints (any type of misdemeanor prior to intake date)
prior_felony Prior number of felony complaints (prior to intake date)
prior_chinsup Prior number of CHINSup complaints (prior to intake date)
prior_chins Prior number of CHINS complaints (prior to intake date)
prior_other_status Prior number of Status complaints (prior to intake date)
prior_other Prior number of other complaints (prior to the intake date)
prior_adj Prior number of adjudicated complaints (FG, G, GA) (prior to intake date)
drg Offense category
description The offense description of the offense.
vcc_code The Virginia Crime Code of the offense.
dai Offense severity of the offense according to the Detention Assessment Instrument (DAI) ranking
flg_category Indicates if the complaint is a technical, status, delinquent, or traffic offense
mso_flag Indicates if the complaint was the most serious offense of the intake case. There may be more than one most serious offense if the severity ranking was tied.
prob_yn Indicates whether the juvenile received probation for the complaint
comm_yn Indicates whether the juvenile was committed to DJJ for the complaint
risk_level The risk level of the youth closest to the intake date based on the Youth Assessment and Screening Instrument (YASI)
ysai_date Indicates if the YASI was done before, on, or after the intake date
assessmenttype Indicates if the YASI is an initial assessment, reassessment, or done at case closure
mentalhealthflag Mental health flag from the YASI
````` ::: :::

### Intake Complaints, Intake Decision Descriptions ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Intake Decision Intake Decision Description
PETITION FILED A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the offense decision was to file a petition.
PETITION/DETENTION ORDER FILED A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the offense decision was to file a petition and issue a detention order.
DETENTION ORDER ONLY Detention order only issued for pre-dispositional cases.
COURT SUMMONS Law enforcement files a court summons directly with the court (e.g., traffic offenses, low-level alcohol/marijuana offenses). In some CSUs, the summons is then entered as a complaint using this offense decision. In other CSUs, the CSU never sees the summons.
PETITION/SHELTER CARE FILED A complaint/affidavit was received and probable cause established. The juvenile requires placement outside the home and secure detention is not appropriate.
UNSUCCESSFUL DIVERSION/PETITION FILED Offense decision on original complaint was to divert. Diversion contract was signed and juvenile violates diversion contract and decision was made (with supervisor approval) to void the diversion and file a petition on the offense.
RESOLVED A complaint was received and the issue was resolved at intake.
SUCCESSFUL DIVERSION The offense decision on an original complaint was to divert. Juvenile successfully completes all obligations of the diversion contract and the intake was closed.
COMPLAINT UNFOUNDED A complaint was received and probable cause could not be established.
UNSUCCESSFUL DIVERSION/NO PETITION FILED The offense decision on an original complaint was to divert. The diversion contract was signed and juvenile violates diversion contract; however, a petition was not filed.
REFERRED TO ANOTHER AGY FOR SV A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the family was referred to another agency for services.
UNOFFICIAL COUNSELING-FAMILY C A complaint was received and the intake officer recommended family counseling to the clients. Follow up by the intake officer is not required.
ACCEPTED VIA ICJ Juvenile was accepted from another state for supervision.
RETURNED TO PROBATION SUPERVIS A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the juvenile was already on probation for another offense. The juvenile will remain on probation and no new action will be taken.
PENDING A complaint was received and probable cause established. This code is for short-term use only. Generally, this is used when the intention is to divert and are awaiting the diversion appointment or when waiting for more information from the police department.
SHELTER CARE ONLY The juvenile was being sent to a non-secure facility or emergency shelter specifically approved to provide a range of as-needed services on an individual basis. See § 16.1-248.1 of the Code of Virginia for additional information.
RETURNED TO OUT-OF-STATE A complaint was received, the juvenile was under supervision in Virginia from another state, and the juvenile was returned to that state.
REQ'D TO PARTICIPATE-DIVERSION A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the complaint was diverted. Diversion is the handling of a juvenile intake compliant in an informal manner rather than through the official court process. The intake officer must develop a plan for the juvenile that may include counseling, informal supervision, restitution, community service, or other programs. The juvenile and his/her parents must agree to the diversion plan. Informal supervision is limited to 90 days for truancy and 120 days for all other offenses. The following complaints may not be diverted: an alleged violent juvenile felony, a complaint after a prior diversion or adjudication on a felony offense, and a second or subsequent truancy complaint. See § 16.1-227 and 16.1- 260 of the Code of Virginia for additional information.
````` ::: :::
